answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The vertex multiplier is published, charged in quill, and velvet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1453 identities would post 4774 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
